view: Q3-26 was a down quarter for Noah's markets: the Shanghai Composite fell 4094 to 3842 and the HSI 25884 to 23294 (Yahoo), and the stock-strategy private funds it distributes were the weakest strategy year-to-date (Simu Paipai via Eastmoney). The rebuild from segment run-rates gives revenue of roughly RMB530-600M against 632.9M a year ago. The run-rates are Q2-26 international wealth management at 88.9M against Q3-25's 146M, insurance shrinking, and Q2's 138M of carry, which is unlikely to repeat. Operating income comes to about 140-170M, and NI to about 130-170M against 218.5M, which had an 84.6M affiliate gain in it. The headline will very likely read down 30% or more year on year. That number sits on top of the stale-looking FY consensus NI (~148M a quarter) and the management margin guide, though, not under it. The JPM cut on Nov-10 and the October underperformance suggest the street had already marked the quarter down. Two swing items cannot be seen beforehand: the mark-to-market on the 'specific listed investment' booked in equity in affiliates (it cost Q1), and any new capital return. On capital return, Noah sits at about 0.7x cash, has a 100% payout record and bought nothing in October. Both could move the stock either way, with an upside tail from a buyback at this discount. The window runs to the next open, and the HK line (6686) prices the release first. This name's opening reactions have been small. I see no line where the price clearly lags, so I make no call.

recommendation.reason: My Q3 rebuild (NI roughly RMB130-170M) lands on the consensus-implied ~148M a quarter and inside management's ~30% full-year margin guide, so the weak quarter looks already marked down. The evidence is the JPM target cut of Nov-10, the stock's 20% fall since September and the FY consensus. The two items that could surprise, the affiliate mark-to-market and a capital-return announcement, cannot be seen before the release and point in opposite directions.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A new large buyback or special dividend at 0.7x cash would push it up. A Q3 operating margin well under 25%, or a big affiliate loss taking GAAP NI under ~100M, would push it down.

self_critique: Against my neutral view on the down side, the quarter could be worse than an FY consensus that looks stale. If Q3 revenue lands near 530M with an affiliate loss, GAAP NI could fall below 100M (-55% yoy), and the Q4-25 profit collapse led to a 12.7% drop, although a day later. On the up side, at 0.7x cash and below a 20% trailing dividend yield, any capital-return line or an op margin above 30% could gap a washed-out stock up in HK before the US open. Neither side shows enough to pass 65%.
approach_notes: P4/P6 helped: splitting the run-in against KWEB/FXI, and checking that the FY consensus already implies a ~30% NI drop, stopped me reading the obvious weak-quarter story as unpriced. The playbook's push to estimate the line from its inputs was hard to apply without a quarterly consensus for a thinly covered foreign filer.
